I opened all 20 screenshots at 1440 (plus the two references) and stacked the nav bars and phone tab bars to compare them. I measured cap heights, card edges, gutters and padding from the pixels and traced each finding to the component that causes it in web/src.

**Where it holds up**
- The profile and feed are very close to profile-1440.png and feed-1440.png.
- Avatar tints for the same person, OrgMark letters, the Unclaimed chip, the count badges and the rail card titles (15px, as in the reference) are consistent across screens.
- In signed-in views the nav active state is correct: Home on feed, Me on the owner profile and availability, Messaging, Notifications, and For employers on the pipeline and post-job pages. Nothing is active on another coach's profile, which is also correct.

**Where it drifts**
The drift sits in the jobs screens and the utility pages, and most of it comes from components built twice:
- two JobCards (feed/JobCard and jobs/JobCard);
- two "Current program" rail cards (profile/RailCards and jobs/ProgramCard);
- two steppers (ClaimStepper and a local one in PostJobForm);
- job stats built with JobHeader's own Fact instead of the shared StatGroup;
- job detail rendered one way in the /jobs pane and another way on /jobs/[id].

**Missing shared pieces**
There is no PageHeader or Breadcrumb component. As a result:
- page titles split into two sizes: 24px on Jobs, Post a job and Pipeline; 16px on Notifications, Messaging, Settings, Claim and Search;
- sub-pages use a breadcrumb, a back link, or nothing.

**Cross-screen data problems**
- Landing says 2,177 coaches; search says 2,185.
- The program staff list shows Ian Falconer as head coach "2010–Present · 17 seasons"; his profile says head coach 2020–Present, 7 seasons.
- Inferred years are dotted on the tree page but not on the profile's tree card.
- Notifications show an unnamed move with an invented "45m"; the feed shows the same kind of event by name with "2026 season".
- Signed-out pages have no nav items at all, so /jobs, /search, program and profile pages show no active state and offer no route to Jobs.

**Smaller rhythm problems**
- Card padding is 16, 24 or 32px depending on the screen, sometimes within one route.
- The jobs list/detail gutter is 12px against 24px everywhere else.
- In messaging, the thread header is inset 8px less than the thread body.
- StatBand numbers are 20px on profile, program and tree, 15px on job pages and 24px on landing.

No issue rises to critical, but 11 findings break §11 rules or the §8 component contracts and are rated major.

findings.where: web/package.json ("next": "15.5.4", react 19.1.0); affects every App Router page, all of which accept Server Action POSTs
findings.problem: The installed Next.js 15.5.4 is affected by GHSA-9qr9-h5gf-34mp (CVE-2025-55182/66478, 'RCE in React flight protocol'). This is a critical bug that lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on the server: Server Action and RSC request bodies are deserialized (decodeReply) before any app code runs. npm audit also lists later critical and high advisories for this version: RSC/Server Action DoS, source-code exposure, cache poisoning, and image-optimizer RCE.
findings.evidence: `node -p "require('./node_modules/next/package.json').version"` gives 15.5.4. `npm audit --omit=dev` gives: next critical, range >=15.5.0-canary.0 <15.5.7, title 'Next.js is vulnerable to RCE in React flight protocol' https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9qr9-h5gf-34mp, plus GHSA-w37m-7fhw-fmv9 (Server Actions source exposure), GHSA-mwv6-3258-q52c / GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf / GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj (Server Components / Server Actions DoS), GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw (image-optimizer RCE <=15.5.27). The attack surface is reachable without a session: any POST to e.g. http://localhost:3000/ with a `Next-Action` header goes through the flight decoder. I did not run an exploit against the shared dev server.
findings.fix: Upgrade next to the latest 15.5.x patch (npm audit names 15.5.28) and react/react-dom to the matching patched 19.1.x. Re-run `npm audit --omit=dev` until it shows no critical/high next advisories. While there, also bump drizzle-orm to >=0.45.2 (GHSA-gpj5-g38j-94v9, identifier escaping). The app builds no identifiers from user input, so that one is not exploitable today.

findings.where: web/src/lib/actions/jobs.ts:19-76 (createJob), :85-109 (closeJob)
findings.problem: Any anonymous visitor can switch to the shared employer demo, a cookie set with no credential. From there they can publish a job listing with free text and external https links. It is permanently public on /jobs, /jobs/[id], the feed and the program page, under a real institution (org ncaa-2751, 'Pacific University (Oregon)'). This is 'write arbitrary data' visible to everyone: phishing links or offensive content shown under a real school's name. Only a 'Sample listing' chip marks it. Messages got per-browser scoping for exactly this reason (the coach demo is a real coach); listings did not. The 25-open-listing cap is per account, and the account is shared by all visitors, so one visitor can fill it and block everyone else. Close-then-repost also allows unlimited total rows. Mass assignment is NOT possible: extra orgId/isDemo/status fields were ignored.
findings.evidence:
Post as the employer. The multipart field 0 must come last, and the action id comes from .next/server/server-reference-manifest.json:
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/employers/jobs/new -b 'cn_demo_session=employer' -H 'Next-Action: 60a179b9e9f0820f1513bfe9dc478f1cb57801c9b2' -H 'Accept: text/x-component' -F '1_title=SECREVIEW test listing' -F '1_roleGroup=head_coach' -F '1_unit=staff' -F '1_employmentType=Full-time' -F '1_description=Arbitrary text any anonymous visitor can publish. Apply at https://evil.example/login now.' -F '1_howToApply=https://evil.example/apply' -F '1_orgId=ncaa-953' -F '1_isDemo=false' -F '0=[null,"$K1"]'
Response: 1:{"errors":{},"published":{"id":37,...}}. DB row: 37|ncaa-2751|Pacific University (Oregon)|is_demo=t|native.
Then signed out: `curl http://localhost:3000/jobs/37` returns 200, and the HTML contains href="https://evil.example/login" and href="https://evil.example/apply". I deleted row 37 afterwards.

Scope them to the authoring browser (a random httpOnly scope cookie, filtered out of public queries), or don't persist them and render the success page from the submitted data. If they must be public, add moderation or allowlisted link domains, a per-IP rate limit, and a TTL. Make the open-listing cap per scope rather than per shared account.

findings.where: web/src/lib/actions/session.ts:6-13 (switchDemoAccount)
findings.problem: Both arguments are client-controlled and unvalidated. `redirectTo` goes straight to redirect(), so the action redirects to absolute and protocol-relative external URLs (open redirect). `role` is written into the session cookie verbatim, so any string works, e.g. '__proto__'; see the session-proto-chain finding. Next's built-in Origin check blocks cross-site invocation, so this is defense-in-depth rather than a remote exploit today. It becomes exploitable as soon as any page passes a URL-derived value (e.g. ?next=) into it.
findings.evidence: curl -s -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/ -H 'Next-Action: 60e44c61b547ea99dc492ab57fcfa28353dffb8fba' -H 'Accept: text/x-component' -H 'Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8' --data-raw '["coach","https://evil.example/phish"]' returns `HTTP/1.1 303`, `x-action-redirect: https://evil.example/phish;push`. With '//evil.example/x' it returns `x-action-redirect: //evil.example/x;push`. With '["__proto__","/about"]' it returns `Set-Cookie: cn_demo_session=__proto__`. The same request with `-H 'Origin: https://evil.example'` returns 500 'Invalid Server Actions request.' (CSRF check works).
findings.fix: Validate with zod: `role: z.enum(["coach","employer","signed_out"])`. Accept redirectTo only if it is a same-origin path: starts with a single '/', does not start with '//' or '/\\', and parses to the same origin with `new URL(v, base)`. Otherwise fall back to '/feed'.

findings.where: web/src/lib/session.ts:22-24 (getSession: `!(role in DEMO_USER_ID)`)
findings.problem: The `in` check walks the prototype chain, so cookie values like '__proto__', 'constructor' and 'toString' pass it. loadDemoSession then calls `DEMO_USER_ID[role]` and gets a non-string. With '__proto__' this throws a TypeError, and every page that calls getSession() without .catch returns 500. switchDemoAccount will set exactly this cookie. The impact is limited to the browser holding the cookie: self-DoS, no cross-user effect.
findings.evidence: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -b 'cn_demo_session=__proto__' http://localhost:3000/settings` returns 500. GET /messaging with the same cookie renders an error boundary with "TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'constructor')" at loadDemoSession (src/lib/session.ts) <- getSession <- MessagingPage.
findings.fix: Use `Object.hasOwn(DEMO_USER_ID, role)`, or a zod enum / literal check (`role === 'coach' || role === 'employer'`), before indexing.

findings.where: web/src/lib/actions/messaging.ts:96-114 (markThreadUnread) and :81-94 (markThreadRead); web/src/lib/queries/shell.ts:9-21 (getShellCounts)
findings.problem: otherUserIn() does not reject '#'-scoped thread ids. When the viewer's id sorts first ('u-demo-ad:u-demo-coach#<scope>'), it returns the bogus other id 'u-demo-coach#<scope>'. markThreadUnread never checks that this user exists, so the employer session can flip a private, per-browser message back to unread. getShellCounts counts every unread message to the user with no scope filter. Result: every visitor using the employer demo sees a phantom unread badge for a message they cannot open or clear. This breaks the documented rule 'saved as read so they never move another visitor's unread badge'. It repeats with a fresh scope each time.
findings.evidence:
1) As coach: POST /messaging Next-Action 40f5a3550c53b4c5118c7d57ab54e30eb2474db27e body [{"threadId":"u-demo-ad:u-demo-coach","body":"x"}]. This returns Set-Cookie cn_demo_scope=16e3fa1b67b97f4406f2eff3 and stores row 9, thread 'u-demo-ad:u-demo-coach#16e3…', read_at set.
2) curl -s -b 'cn_demo_session=employer; cn_demo_scope=16e3fa1b67b97f4406f2eff3' -X POST http://localhost:3000/messaging -H 'Next-Action: 4073bcd67599a15e7ead3c1743e39ae02e8d2bcd5b' -H 'Accept: text/x-component' -H 'Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8' --data-raw '["u-demo-ad:u-demo-coach#16e3fa1b67b97f4406f2eff3"]' returns 1:{"ok":true}. The AD's unread count goes from 1 to 2.
3) A fresh employer visitor with no scope cookie: GET /notifications shows aria-label="Messaging, 2 unread", but the thread is invisible to them. I deleted the row afterwards.
findings.fix: Have otherUserIn (or the actions) reject ids containing '#', and require the other id to exist in users. Have markThread{Read,Unread} operate on `threadId` plus `scopedThreadId(threadId, readDemoScope())` only. Apply visibleTo(scope) in getShellCounts too.

findings.where: web/src/lib/actions/messaging.ts:22-35,57-68 (sendMessage rate limit / ensureDemoScope)
findings.problem: The 20-messages-per-10-minutes limit is keyed on the client-supplied cn_demo_scope cookie. A client that drops the cookie gets a new scope, and a new quota, on every request, so the database can be filled without bound (2000 chars per row). sendMessage also opens brand-new threads with any existing user, e.g. employer to u-demo-avery or u-demo-dana, which the UI never offers. The scoping now hides these from other visitors, but they still add DB writes.
findings.evidence: 22 POSTs in a row without returning the scope cookie, each: curl -s -b 'cn_demo_session=coach' -X POST http://localhost:3000/messaging -H 'Next-Action: 40f5a3550c53b4c5118c7d57ab54e30eb2474db27e' -H 'Accept: text/x-component' -H 'Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8' --data-raw '[{"threadId":"u-demo-ad:u-demo-coach","body":"SECREVIEW rl N"}]'. Result: accepted=22/22 within 10 minutes; the DB shows 22 rows across 22 distinct scopes. Before scoping was added, an employer POST with threadId 'u-demo-ad:u-demo-avery' also created a new thread (row 7). All test rows deleted.
findings.fix: Rate-limit on a server-side key: client IP or IP+UA at the edge or in a middleware token bucket, plus a global cap on demo writes. Only allow sendMessage into threads that already have an unscoped seeded row, or into an explicit allowlist of demo counterparts.

Concurrent calls (double-click, retries, two tabs on the shared demo) create duplicate candidates at the same position. submitClaim has the same select-then-insert pattern on claims without a unique (person_id, user_id).
findings.evidence: Six parallel calls of POST /employers/pipeline, Next-Action 6093cab0d29001009f4820b2f0d359d2c3a88cb431, body ["p-zbig-kepa",1], cookie cn_demo_session=employer. findings.fix: Add uniqueIndex on shortlist_entries(shortlist_id, person_id) and use `.onConflictDoNothing().returning()` (then re-select on conflict). Do the same for claims(person_id, user_id) with onConflictDoUpdate.

findings.where: web/src/lib/actions/employer.ts:198-225 (restoreCandidate); messaging.ts:81,97 (markThreadRead/Unread threadId); search.ts:110 (requestConnection personId); program.ts:81 (setProgramFollow follow)
findings.problem: Several actions trust the declared TypeScript types, but Server Action arguments are arbitrary JSON. restoreCandidate never checks that personId exists and leaves position unbounded, so it inserts into the DB and fails with an FK or int4-overflow error: unhandled 500, and in dev the SQL text leaks in the error. markThreadRead/Unread call threadId.split on non-strings (500). setProgramFollow echoes a non-boolean `follow`. search.requestConnection has no zod schema for personId. These fail safe for authorization, but give 500s and noisy logs.
findings.evidence: restoreCandidate (employer, Next-Action 4013d4001b100ff7c41a09c4510cf3dfb4211f6e6b) with [{"shortlistId":1,"personId":"does-not-exist","stage":"sourced","note":null,"position":0}] returns HTTP 500 'Failed query: insert into "shortlist_entries" ...'. With position 9999999999 it returns HTTP 500 the same way. markThreadRead (coach, 40f4e366743cefebf9215129e40a74912e17e4fbaa) with [123] returns HTTP 500 'threadId.split is not a function'. setProgramFollow (60ab07f18e9a2565df2df8d512244df53c3f2ba81a) with ["ncaa-2751",{"x":1}] returns {"ok":true,"following":"$T0:1"}.
findings.fix: Parse every action's arguments with zod at the top: z.string().max(200) for ids/threadIds, z.boolean() for follow, position .max(1_000_000) as moveCandidate does. In restoreCandidate, verify the person exists (as addToPipeline does). Wrap inserts in try/catch and return {ok:false}.

findings.where: web/src/app/programs/[slug]/page.tsx:69-74 (siteOrigin) -> canonical, og:url, ProgramJsonLd; web/src/app/in/[slug]/tree/page.tsx:41-49 (inviteHref)
findings.problem: The absolute origin is built from the client-controlled X-Forwarded-Host / Host headers. It is written into <link rel=canonical>, og:url, JSON-LD url fields and the tree page's mailto invite body. Behind a shared cache or CDN that forwards X-Forwarded-Host but does not key on it, this allows cache poisoning (SEO hijack, or links pointing to an attacker's host).
findings.evidence: curl -s -H 'X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example' http://localhost:3000/programs/adrian | grep canonical gives `<link rel="canonical" href="http://evil.example/programs/adrian"/>`, `og:url content="http://evil.example/programs/adrian"` and JSON-LD `"url":"http://evil.example/programs/adrian"`.
findings.fix: Use a configured site origin (e.g. NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL / metadataBase) instead of request headers. Or trust X-Forwarded-Host only from a known proxy and validate it against an allowlist.

findings.where: web/src/app/dev/components/page.tsx:11-18 (loadDemoSession('coach') for signed-out viewers); components/shell/MeMenu.tsx:81-82
findings.problem: /dev/components is public, with no NODE_ENV or session gate. It loads the coach demo session without a cookie and renders its Me menu, including the private 'Open to opportunities' status. The demo coach is a real, non-demo person (p-justin-leatherman, is_demo=f). Any visitor can switch to the coach demo and turn the setting on, and the gallery then broadcasts e.g. 'On · visible to employers except Pacific (OR)' under his name to anyone. The schema comment says this setting is never shown publicly.
findings.evidence: `curl -s http://localhost:3000/dev/components` (no cookie) returns 200. The HTML contains `Open to opportunitiesOff · only you see this`, rendered from the availability row for p-justin-leatherman.
findings.fix: Gate /dev/* behind `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` (notFound()) or an env flag, and render the gallery with the FALLBACK_VIEWER fixture instead of a live session.

findings.where: web/next.config.ts (no headers()); web/src/lib/actions/session.ts:12, messaging.ts:33, program.ts:94 (cookie options)
findings.problem: There are no security headers. CSP, frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options (clickjacking on one-click actions such as Close listing and demo switch), X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy are all missing, and X-Powered-By: Next.js is sent. The cn_demo_session, cn_demo_scope and cn_follows cookies are httpOnly and SameSite=Lax but lack Secure.
findings.evidence: `curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://localhost:3000/about` shows only Vary, link, Cache-Control, X-Powered-By: Next.js, Content-Type. The set-cookie seen above: `cn_demo_session=coach; Path=/; ...; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax` (no Secure).
findings.fix: Add headers() in next.config.ts: Content-Security-Policy (with frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin. Set poweredByHeader: false. Add `secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` to every cookies().set.

findings.where: All server actions in web/src/lib/actions/*.ts; web/src/app/api/typeahead/route.ts
findings.problem: (Note only.) Apart from the cookie-keyed message limit, nothing is rate limited. Unbounded writes include createJob via close/repost, submitClaim (one row per person per user, so thousands of rows with arbitrary emails kept forever), saveCandidateNote and addToPipeline. Unauthenticated reads (/api/typeahead, findPrograms) run leading-wildcard ILIKE scans across people/organizations.
findings.evidence: Code review: no middleware.ts and no limiter anywhere in src. /api/typeahead and the findPrograms action (4093ae9ba14d4931236717a0ddb25f188af41f1c31) respond to signed-out requests; e.g. findPrograms with ["%"] returns [] (wildcards escaped, but no throttling).
findings.fix: Add an edge/middleware token-bucket limit per IP for POSTs with a Next-Action header and for /api/typeahead. Add TTL cleanup for demo-authored claims, pipeline notes and listings.

2.summary:
Reviewed every Server Action in web/src/lib/actions/*.ts, the only route handler (src/app/api/typeahead/route.ts), and both session modules. The messaging code was being edited by another agent during the review; the messaging findings are against the latest version (per-browser scopes). Every test request ran against http://localhost:3000. I replayed Server Actions with curl, using action ids taken from .next/server/server-reference-manifest.json. All test rows were deleted afterwards (messages, shortlist entries, job 37).

What I found:
- **Critical:** next 15.5.4 is affected by the React flight protocol RCE (GHSA-9qr9-h5gf-34mp) and other critical/high advisories. Upgrade to the latest 15.5.x (npm audit names 15.5.28).
- **Major:** any anonymous visitor can switch to the shared employer demo and publish a permanent public job listing with arbitrary text and https links under a real school (Pacific University (Oregon)). Signed-out visitors can see it. One visitor can also use up the shared 25-listing cap.
- **Minor, all demonstrated:**
  - Open redirect plus an unvalidated role in switchDemoAccount. Cross-site use is blocked by Next's Origin check.
  - A `__proto__` session cookie passes the `in` check in getSession and returns 500 on every session page.
  - markThreadUnread accepts '#'-scoped thread ids, and the nav badge count ignores scope. So the employer session can create a phantom unread badge that every employer visitor sees and nobody can clear.
  - The message rate limit is keyed on a client cookie: 22 of 22 messages were accepted after dropping it.
  - addToPipeline has a check-then-insert race: 6 parallel calls created 3 duplicate entries (no unique index; claims has the same pattern).
  - Missing argument validation causes 500s: restoreCandidate (FK error, int overflow), markThreadRead with a non-string id, setProgramFollow.
  - X-Forwarded-Host is written into canonical, og:url and JSON-LD.
  - /dev/components is public and shows the real demo coach's private availability status.
  - There are no security headers, and cookies lack Secure.
  - Rate limiting is absent everywhere else (note only).

What holds up:
- **SQL:** every query is parameterized through drizzle sql`` and operators. The only sql.raw is the constant '#'. escapeLike is applied on every live ILIKE path. The one unescaped ILIKE is in the unused listJobs (src/lib/queries/jobs.ts:17, tests only).
- **HTML rendering:** no user text reaches dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Both JSON-LD blocks escape '<'. Job descriptions are parsed into plain data and rendered as React text, links are made only for http(s) URLs, and emails always get a mailto: prefix. Message bodies and notes render as plain text.
- **Who can do what:** signed-out and coach sessions cannot post or close jobs or touch the pipeline. The employer cannot save availability. closeJob refuses other programs' listings. Shortlist ownership and thread membership are enforced, and signed-out sendMessage is refused.
- **Mass assignment:** extra orgId, isDemo and status fields on createJob were ignored.
- **CSRF:** Next's Origin check rejects cross-origin action calls ('Invalid Server Actions request.'), cookies are httpOnly and SameSite=Lax, and no GET request has side effects.

findings.problem: yearsExplicit is true, but the bio never gives a year for the Greensboro stint. 2015 is worked out from his graduation year plus the duration 'a year'. The org, role, sport and the year itself look right; only the flag overstates how the year was sourced.

The evidence quote has no year. resolve.py years_explicit() only downgrades the flag when the DURATION regex matches, and that regex (resolve.py:673-676) needs a digit or a number word, so 'a year' / 'a season' slips past the downgrade.
findings.fix: Set yearsExplicit=false for this row. Add 'a|an' to the quantifier in DURATION (or NUMBER_WORDS) so phrases like 'spent a year' / 'a season' trigger the downgrade, then re-run resolve and the years_explicit tests.

findings.evidence: Bio: 'Wolf is one of the top kicking/punting coaches in the country as well as founder and clinical director of Wolf Kicking.' resolve.py:1518 builds every bio row with "isCurrent": False, and only choose_current() sets it to True, for one row. findings.fix: Have the extractor emit an is_current flag, or treat present-tense evidence ('is', 'serves as', 'currently') as current, and let isCurrent be true on more than one row. Otherwise, document that isCurrent means 'primary current roster role' only.
